headline: Voters approved $4.5 million for a Neary School roof replacement, while town boards finalized major borrowing articles and the FY27 operating budget.
synopsis: March was dominated by Special Town Meeting action and preparations for the April 11 Annual Town Meeting. Voters at the March 2 Special Town Meeting approved $4.5 million in borrowing to replace the Margaret A. Neary Elementary School roof and $175,000 for a renovation feasibility study, while decisively rejecting proposals to study consolidating into Trottier and Finn schools. Town boards subsequently prepared for Annual Town Meeting, with the Select Board endorsing a $25 million 20-year borrowing article for town roads and sidewalks in a divided 3-2 vote. Officials also advanced an $8.83 million borrowing article to replace Trottier Middle School's roof through a state reimbursement program, while postponing an estimated $800,000 cleanup of the Atwood water tank property to the fall. Meanwhile, the Advisory Committee and Select Board finalized recommendations for the FY27 municipal budget, which projects an operating budget exceeding $71 million.

top_items.title: Neary School roof replacement approved at Special Town Meeting
top_items.why: Voters authorized $4.5 million to replace the Neary Elementary School roof and $175,000 for a renovation study, while rejecting school consolidation plans.
top_items.body: At the March 2 Special Town Meeting, voters approved Article 4 by a 377-33 vote, authorizing $4.5 million in borrowing to replace Neary Elementary School's failing roof during summer 2026, subject to a subsequent ballot vote. Voters also approved $175,000 under Article 1 to fund a feasibility study evaluating a modernization or code-compliance renovation. By contrast, alternative articles to spend over $800,000 studying additions at Trottier and Finn to decommission Neary were rejected by wide margins. Following the vote, the Select Board and School Committee created a five-member Elementary School Building Committee and appointed members Robert Moss, Andrew Pfaff, and Jason Malinowski.

top_items.title: Select Board endorses $25 million road and sidewalk borrowing
top_items.why: The Select Board voted 3-2 to support a 20-year, $25 million capital borrowing authorization for Annual Town Meeting.
top_items.body: On March 31, the Select Board voted 3-2 to recommend Article 13 on the Annual Town Meeting warrant, which authorizes $25 million in borrowing over 20 years to fund the DPW's five-year pavement plan covering 33 miles of road and four new sidewalk projects. The board debated whether to scale the initial request down to $10 million to $17 million to avoid borrowing for shorter-lived preventative maintenance under the town's debt policy. The Capital Improvement and Planning Committee deferred taking a formal stance until Town Meeting.

top_items.title: Town boards back $8.83 million Trottier roof replacement
top_items.why: Officials unanimously advanced an $8.83 million roof replacement for Trottier Middle School to the Annual Town Meeting warrant.
top_items.body: Assistant Superintendent Keith LaVoie presented details for replacing Trottier Middle School's 1998 roof, which has suffered from leaks and buckled substrate. The Massachusetts School Building Authority will reimburse 41.32 percent of eligible costs under its Accelerated Repair Program, leaving Southborough with an estimated net cost of $5.39 million to be funded by a Proposition 2 1/2 debt exclusion. The Select Board, School Committee, Advisory Committee, and Capital Improvement and Planning Committee all voted unanimously to support Article 15.

top_items.title: Boards recommend FY27 operating budget heading to Town Meeting
top_items.why: The Advisory Committee and Select Board recommended an FY27 operating budget carrying an estimated tax increase under 5 percent.
top_items.body: Town boards finalized their positions on Article 6 for the FY27 operating budget. The Advisory Committee voted 5-0 to recommend a town budget of $73,455,973 (including capital items), projecting a 4.64 percent tax increase and an available levy balance of $553,000. The Select Board tentatively supported the operating budget in a split 3-2 vote after shifting vehicle purchases and health insurance costs, with some members arguing for flat municipal headcounts. The School Committee closed its hearing on a $26.11 million K-8 operational budget, up 3.99 percent over FY26, and the Regional School Committee closed its hearing on a $31.42 million budget.

top_items.title: Industrial Park zoning amendments proposed for Town Meeting
top_items.why: Planning officials advanced a comprehensive overhaul of 40-year-old Industrial Park zoning bylaws to add performance standards and regulate data centers.
top_items.body: Planning Board hearings continued on Article 17, which overhauls the town's Industrial Park district rules. The proposal establishes performance standards for noise, vibration, and odors, incorporates state standards for small clean energy installations, and creates a special permit framework for data centers capped at 50,000 square feet with a 1,000-foot buffer setback from residential and conservation parcels. The Select Board voted 4-0-1 to support the article, while the Planning Board and Advisory Committee scheduled final reviews just before Town Meeting.

top_items.title: Atwood site soil cleanup delayed to fall Special Town Meeting
top_items.why: Select Board and Advisory Committee opted to defer an estimated $800,000 to $850,000 soil remediation article to the fall.
top_items.body: DPW Director Bill Cundiff and environmental consultants presented options to remediate lead-contaminated soil at the former Atwood Road water tank site to state standards. The Advisory Committee and Select Board agreed to postpone the borrowing appropriation to the fall Special Town Meeting so residents can review intended future uses for the parcel before authorizing cleanup funds. As a result, current procurement bids were canceled, and the item was removed from the spring Annual Town Meeting warrant.

top_items.title: Select Board and Advisory back appointed Town Clerk proposal
top_items.why: Town boards voted unanimously to support converting the Town Clerk position from an elected role to an appointed position.
top_items.body: Town Clerk Jim Hegarty presented Article 25 to convert the Town Clerk from an elected official to an appointed position, citing increasing statutory election complexities and the need to recruit qualified candidates beyond town residents. Both the Select Board (5-0) and the Advisory Committee (5-0) voted to recommend the measure to Town Meeting voters, where it would require local approval followed by either a ballot question or state legislative action.
